newsitem.title: ITALY: SanPaolo wants end-April private placement.
newsitem.headline: SanPaolo wants end-April private placement.

text.p: Italian bank San Paolo said on Monday it aimed to make a private placement of a total stake of 20 percent in the bank by the end of April.
San Paolo chairman Gianni Zandano told a news conference the banking group also wanted to make a public share sale offer (OPV) of 25 percent of the bank in the first half of 1997.
On the question of the public offer, Zandano said: "We cannot go much beyond the first half (of 1997) and we hope to complete it within the first half if possible."
Talking about the private placement, Zandano said the bank was aiming to form a stable core of foreign and Italian shareholders, none of whom would hold more than five percent of the bank.
The private placement involving the stable shareholders of 20 percent of the bank's capital would be completed by the end of April, he said.
The entire operation would reduce the stake in the bank held by San Paolo Holding from 65 percent at present to no more than 20 percent.
